access.edition_or_version: Composed 1258; public-domain English translations include James Ross (1900) and Edward Eastwick

mechanics.reader_promise: Affectionate moral counsel: hard truths offered as a friend's advice, made palatable with wit.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person narrator who reports encounters and dialogues as personal anecdotes and travel memory.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Friendly middle distance: the narrator is experienced and advising, but not elevated above the reader.
mechanics.dialogue: Embedded conversations and anecdotes carry the instruction; wisdom arrives through exchange rather than lecture.
mechanics.style_and_devices: adab prose alternating with aphoristic verse; humour and anecdote softening instruction; 'bitter medicine mixed with the honey of wit' per Sa'di's own framing.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Repeated pattern of encounter -> counsel -> aphoristic crystallisation, cumulatively bonding narrator and reader.
mechanics.tone_markers: Counsel-as-friendship, inclusive humour, plain elegant prose, avoidance of preachiness.
